tagline: Down the barrier islands and over the sound by ferry.
intro: From Whalebone Junction NC 12 runs south down the barrier islands, Bodie and Pea and Hatteras, with Pamlico Sound in view to the west, through Rodanthe and Buxton to the ferry at Hatteras Inlet. A free ferry crosses to Ocracoke. A second, about two and a quarter hours over the sound, lands at Cedar Island, and the road goes on through the fishing villages Down East toward Beaufort.
The junction got its name in the early 1930s, when Alexander Midgett hauled a 72-foot whale skeleton there in the back of his Model T to drum up trade at his filling station. It worked.

moments.title: Cape Hatteras Lighthouse
moments.text: The tallest masonry lighthouse in the country, 208 feet of black and white stripe, was moved 2,900 feet inland in 1999, when the sea had come within 15 feet of it.

moments.title: Ocracoke Light
moments.text: Built in 1823 by Silver Lake in Ocracoke village, the oldest operating light station in the state, near the inlet where Blackbeard was killed in 1718.

moments.title: Atlantic
moments.text: Old workboats fill the harbor on Core Sound, in a village that has long fished for its living and keeps one fish house still working.

practical: The Hatteras Inlet ferry is free and takes about 40 minutes. The Cedar Island ferry charges a toll, takes about 2.25 hours, and reservations are recommended. Storms have breached NC 12 many times between Oregon Inlet and Rodanthe and on Ocracoke, closing it for days or months.
